method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and copied Table 1 row segments (row label through the patient's column) as spans; every span was checked verbatim against the paper. Table 1 has patients as columns; header row: 'Clinical features | Patient B | Patient C | Caldeira et al., 2005 | Stockler et al., 2014 | Mahmutoglu et al., 2014'. Patients B and C keep their own labels; the three previously published patients with c.506G>A are labelled 'Table 1 column 3/4/5' with the column header copied into source_reference_in_review. Relatives: parents of Patient A ('heterozygous carrier status in parents') and the parents of Patients B and C ('their parents were confirmed to be carriers') get rows as 'parent of Patient A (2)' and 'parent of Patient B (2)' (they are parents of both sisters; Patient B was the sister sequenced first). Sex of parents not stated. Inheritance: for the homozygous probands both parents are stated carriers; the enum has no biallelic/biparental value, so 'inherited unspecified parent' was used. Parents of B and C are 'carriers' without a stated zygosity, so zygosity is not reported. For Patient C and all parents, transcript, protein, type and pathogenicity come from the sentence describing this exact variant in the index patient. For the literature patients only c.506G>A and 'pathogenic' (Table 1 title) were filled; transcript, protein and variant type left not reported. Ages: Patient A is called 'A 3.6-year-old boy [who] presented', but the text also says he 'presented at 1 year of age' and was 3.6 years after 1 year of treatment; 3.6 years was taken as the last evaluation and converted literally to P3.6Y (it may mean 3 years 6 months). Patients B/C onset recorded from text '8–10 months of age' (named group 'Both'); Table 1 gives onset 1 year (row 'Age onset/diagnosis (years)'), diagnosis 10 and 8 years. Literature onset '-' for Stockler is not reported. 'Age/origin' was taken as age at last evaluation for every column. Normal investigations: whole-study normals (normal MRI brain, normal tone, 'Movement disorder: No') were recorded as excluded rows naming the investigation; per D-27 a normal MRI does not exclude the specific MRI checklist items, and 'Movement disorder: No' does not exclude dystonia, ataxia, chorea or tremor. 'Normal tone' was taken to exclude hypotonia but not spasticity. 'Epilepsy: No' (Patient B, Stockler, Mahmutoglu) was recorded as an excluded feature row but left 'not reported' for the broader checklist item 'seizures or epilepsy'. Patient A's normal auditory brainstem response was recorded as a feature but hearing loss left not reported. Possible tension: Patient A had 'no history of looseness or tightness of the body' yet examination found 'truncal hypotonia'; treated as history vs examination rather than a contradiction, so hypotonia is observed. Group statements about the two sisters ('Both', 'They') are marked 'inferred from group statement'; Table 1 per-column cells are 'stated for this individual'. Abnormal laboratory values without an explicit statement of abnormality (e.g. plasma creatinine 0.034, GAA 27, urine creatinine) were not recorded. Vital status not stated explicitly for anyone. No stacked cells. Paper cites no earlier publication of its own patients (field left null).
